A PMOS input pair cannot work at a 0.9 V CM because |Vth| is ~1 V, so the input pair is NMOS biased at high gm/Id. Matching RC time constants (R1C1 = RfCf) cancels the input-node pole. Budget: about 62 uA tail plus IREF, under 86 uA at 1.98 V. vcm on the + input sets the 0.9 V output."}

PARAMS = {
    "W_in":  (16.0, 4.0, 60.0),     # input pair width [um] (high gm/Id, weak/moderate inversion)
    "L_in":  (0.20, 0.15, 0.5),
    "W_ld":  (8.0, 2.0, 30.0),      # PMOS mirror load width [um]
    "L_ld":  (0.30, 0.15, 0.6),
    "W_tu":  (4.0, 1.0, 20.0),      # tail-mirror unit width [um]
    "L_t":   (0.5, 0.3, 1.0),
    "I_tail": (62e-6, 30e-6, 70e-6),# tail current target -> integer mirror ratio vs IREF
    "Rf":    (50e3, 20e3, 200e3),
    "ratio": (0.1175, 0.105, 0.125),# Rf/R1 (pre-distorted for finite loop gain)
    "Cf":    (300e-15, 60e-15, 1e-12),
}

def _vgs_for(lut, dev, W, L, Id, vds, vsb=0.0):
    lo, hi = 0.2, 1.8
    for _ in range(50):
        mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
        if lut.op(dev, W, L, mid, vds, vsb)["Id"] < Id:
            lo = mid
        else:
            hi = mid
    return 0.5 * (lo + hi)

def design(p, lut, spec):
    vdd = 1.8
    vcm = spec.get("vcm", 0.9)
    iref = spec.get("iref", 10e-6)
    cl = spec.get("cl", 200e-15)

    # ---- mirror ratio for tail current, capped by power budget at 1.98 V ----
    i_max = 170e-6 / 1.98 * 0.92 - iref
    i_t = min(p["I_tail"], i_max)
    best = None
    for mr in range(1, 9):
        mt = max(1, int(round(mr * i_t / iref)))
        it = iref * mt / mr
        if it + iref > 170e-6 / 1.98 * 0.95:
            mt = max(1, int(math.floor(mr * i_t / iref)))
            it = iref * mt / mr
        err = abs(it - i_t)
        if best is None or err < best[0]:
            best = (err, mr, mt, it)
    _, mr, mt, itail = best
    Wref = p["W_tu"] * mr
    Wtail = p["W_tu"] * mt
    Lt = p["L_t"]

    # ---- feedback network (RfCf = R1C1 cancels input-node pole) ----
    Rf = p["Rf"]
    R1 = Rf / p["ratio"]
    Cf = p["Cf"]
    C1 = Cf * Rf / R1

    n = Netlist("vin1 vin2 vout vcm vdd vss ibias")
    # bias
    n.M("MREF", "ibias", "ibias", "vss", "vss", "nfet", Wref, Lt)
    n.M("MT", "tail", "ibias", "vss", "vss", "nfet", Wtail, Lt)
    # input pair: M1 (+ input, vcm) on diode side, M2 (- input, vn) on output side
    n.M("M1", "d1", "vcm", "tail", "vss", "nfet", p["W_in"], p["L_in"])
    n.M("M2", "vout", "vn", "tail", "vss", "nfet", p["W_in"], p["L_in"])
    # PMOS mirror load
    n.M("M3", "d1", "d1", "vdd", "vdd", "pfet", p["W_ld"], p["L_ld"])
    n.M("M4", "vout", "d1", "vdd", "vdd", "pfet", p["W_ld"], p["L_ld"])
    # feedback
    n.R("R1", "vin1", "vn", R1)
    n.C("C1", "vin1", "vn", C1)
    n.R("RF", "vout", "vn", Rf)
    n.C("CF", "vout", "vn", Cf)
    n.R("RX", "vin2", "vcm", 1e9)   # vin2 unused (benign tie)

    # ---- first-order predictions (TT, 27C) ----
    ib = itail / 2
    vgs_in = _vgs_for(lut, "n", p["W_in"], p["L_in"], ib, 0.6)
    vtail = vcm - vgs_in
    o_in = lut.op("n", p["W_in"], p["L_in"], vgs_in, vdd - 1.0 - vtail + 0.1, 0.0)
    vsg_ld = _vgs_for(lut, "p", p["W_ld"], p["L_ld"], ib, 0.9)
    o_ld = lut.op("p", p["W_ld"], p["L_ld"], vsg_ld, vdd - vcm)
    gm1, gds1 = o_in["gm"], o_in["gds"]
    gm3, gds4 = o_ld["gm"], o_ld["gds"]
    gload = 1.0 / (Rf + R1)
    A = gm1 / (gds1 + gds4 + gload)
    beta = R1 / (R1 + Rf)
    cin = o_in["cgg"]
    beta_hf = Cf / (Cf + C1 + cin)
    ideal = Rf / R1
    a1 = -ideal / (1.0 + 1.0 / (A * beta))
    cser = Cf * (C1 + cin) / (Cf + C1 + cin)
    cout = cl + cser + 0.6 * o_in["cgg"] * 0.3 + 0.5 * o_ld["cgg"] * 0.3
    bw = gm1 * beta_hf / (2 * PI * cout)
    # mirror-pole correction (pole-zero doublet)
    fp2 = gm3 / (2 * PI * (2 * o_ld["cgg"] + 0.3 * o_in["cgg"]))
    bw = bw / math.sqrt(1 + (bw / (2 * fp2)) ** 2)
    power = vdd * (iref + itail)
    vout_offset = 0.9 * 0 + (1.0 / beta) * (0.2 / max(A, 1)) * 0.05  # systematic only, small

    return n, {"a1": a1, "a2": 0.0, "bw": bw, "vout_offset": vout_offset,
               "power": power, "loop_gain": A * beta, "vtail": vtail,
               "mirror_ratio": mt / mr}
